They found smudged fingerprints on the scissors besides the anti-theft tags that couldn't be used to identify or not identify Ms. Armstrong.
 The store assistant claims she heard scissors being used inside of the dressing room, and identified Ms. Armstrong as the woman who left that dressing room.
The store has camera footage of Ms. Armstrong exiting the dressing room and returning the dress to a rack.
Ms. Armstrong has a strong reputation.

A digital evidence expert testified that they saw Ms. Garcia leaving the hospital with a baby in her arms on the camera footage.
A nurse testified that they saw Ms. Garcia on a different floor with a patient at the time the alarm went off to notify a baby was missing.
Evidence from a bathroom near an emergency exit matched Ms. Garcia's DNA.
A prominent leader in the community testified that he believes Ms. Garcia is a trustworthy person.

The bullets recovered from the neighbor's yard do not match the bullets test-fired from Mr. Anderson's only gun.
In a recorded 911 call from Mr. Anderson's house, someone can be heard saying if you don't do something about the party  I will."
A person from the neighborhood has testified that Mr. Anderson has a non-violent history.
A woman from the party recalled seeing someone from an open window across from Mr. Anderson's house with a gun."

They went through Ms. Franklin's business records for her two legitimate businesses, as well as her personal documents and tax records, and found nothing related to the fake company.
An employee for Ms. Franklin has testified that she's a trustworthy person.
An insurance agent who works in the same building as the fake company testified that they saw people in the fake company's office, but never Ms. Franklin.
They found a fingerprint that matches Ms. Franklin's on one of the fake company's documents.

They found selfies on Mr. Juval's phone of him drinking wine at a bar two miles away from the crash site.
A victim who was knocked over by the fleeing vehicle testified that it could have been Mr. Juval, but could've been someone else.
An expert testified that a palm print found on the driver's side door matches Mr. Juval's.
Mr. Juval was previously convicted 5 years ago of assault on construction workers.

Torn packaging was found in the fitting room with prints that matched the defendants.
The defendant's employees have testified that in their opinion, she was prone to theft.
The cashier working at the time of the theft claims the defendant was not the woman who purchased the chocolate milk, peanut butter, and raisin bread.
Investigators recovered a time-stamped reciept from Target with chocolate milk, peanut butter, and raisin bread in the defendant's apartment.

A reciept for a five-gallon gas can was found in Mr. Farqooih's residence, the same gas can that was left in the fire.
Mr. Farqooih's ex-employer testified that Mr. Farqooih was not a law-abiding person.
An investigator testified that no fingerprints at the scene matched Mr. Farqooih's.
An eyewitness saw someone later identified as Mr. Farqooih near the building with a gas can.

Mr. Johnson was previously convicted of forgery of false documents.
An expert was able to match DNA evidence from a soda can dropped off from the driver of a van that pulled off as soon as a state trooper pulled in.
An eyewitness claims that Mr. Johnson is the same man who handed an envelope to the driver of a 16-passenger van at a rest stop.
No phone calls, emails, or text messages were able to be tracked from Mr. Johnson's phone/computer to Mexico.

A zoning board clerk claims that they saw a person later identified as Mr. Jackson hand an envelope (the same kind as the bribe envelope) to the voting officials prior to voting.
DNA from the sealed flap of the bribe envelope cannot be matched to Mr. Jackson.
Mr. Jackson was previously convicted for failing to pay his taxes.
From bank records and a deed of sale, Mr. Jackson sold his 34-foot boat for $43,000 three weeks prior to the voting.

A guest at the store claims that while checking out the guest before her, Ms. Clarke did not ring up all of the items she bagged.
Out of all the stolen items recovered, none of the fingerprints could be matched to Ms. Clarke.
Ms. Clarke's priest says that she has a reputation for honesty within the church community.
Security camera footage doesn't show Ms. Clarke obviously bagging items without hitting buttons on the register first.
